editorial:
Imagine being the most popular guy in school and suddenly losing your girlfriend. That is exactly what happens to Berke, a basketball star who thinks his world is ending when Allison dumps him. To get her back, he does the unthinkable: he joins the school play. He is totally out of his element, but he gets help from Kelly, his best friend's sister. The whole thing feels like a classic high school romp with a funny twist because the play they are putting on is actually based on Shakespeare. It is a lighthearted ride that captures that awkward feeling of trying too hard to impress someone who has already moved on.

You will love the chemistry between the leads and how the movie pokes fun at high school stereotypes. While the plot is pretty predictable, the pacing keeps things moving quickly so you never get bored. If you enjoy cheesy romantic comedies from the early 2000s, you should definitely give this a go. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a digital rental on Apple TV to get the best picture. If you are a collector, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this feel-good movie handy for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: During the final performance of the play, Berke realizes that he does not actually want Allison back. He spends the whole movie trying to win her over, but he discovers that his feelings for Kelly are much stronger. He ends up confessing his love for Kelly right there at school. The movie wraps up with Berke and Kelly becoming a couple, finally moving past the old drama and starting a new, happier relationship together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves early 2000s teen comedies and cute love stories.
